summary: Custom claim encoding strips role suffix in on-prem proxy, causing partial RBAC bindings
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that some admin users in their private on-prem deployment intermittently lose admin permissions. Root cause appears to be that a custom identity provider includes a namespaced role claim that contains an encoded delimiter (e.g., 'team%2Fadmin' or 'svc+ops-admin'). When the assertion traverses their on-prem ingress proxy, the claim value is being decoded/normalized and the suffix (after the delimiter) is removed before Redwood's RBAC mapping runs, resulting in 'team' or 'svc' being matched instead of 'team/admin' or 'svc+ops-admin'. Impact: selected admin users are downgraded to tenant-level roles causing failed admin operations (403) in the Console and Admin API.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer issues an auth assertion from IdP with claim 'x-roles: team%2Fadmin,svc+ops-admin'
2) Assertion sent through on-prem ingress (NGINX-based) to private control plane via X-Auth-Assertion header
3) Redwood's auth pipeline receives header and runs claim namespace sanitizer and RBAC mapping
4) Observe that mapped roles are 'team' and 'svc' (suffix removed), user lacks admin bindings
logs: RBAC decision denied: missing role binding 'team/admin' -> http 403 admin API
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: IdP claim encoding mismatch vs Redwood claim sanitizer. Customer asserts they send encoded values by design.
Reproduced in customer's staging by curling ingress with encoded claim header; observed ingress decodes %2F to '/' and then downstream sanitizer splits on '/' leaving only prefix.
Ingress (NGINX) config had 'underscores_in_headers on;' and a header decode step in custom lua middleware that calls ngx.unescape_uri on incoming assertion headers.

Redwood RBAC mapping expects namespace delimiter to be preserved (we canonicalize on raw claim value). When ingress decodes and then downstream sanitizer further normalizes, trailing segments after certain delimiters are dropped by our current 'namespace-split' sanitizer implementation.
SRE confirmed the on-prem ingress behavior differs from hosted edge where headers arrive still percent-encoded in most customer setups.
Log correlation: timestamps line up with support ticket; affected users are those with claims containing encoded delimiters (%, +, /).
comments: Customer (Maya R.): We're seeing ~4-6% of our admin workforce intermittently lose access after SSO login since the proxy upgrade last week. We scoped to users with roles containing '/'.
Support (Leah): Thanks, Maya — can you share a redacted X-Auth-Assertion header? Also please confirm ingress type and version.
Customer (Maya): Provided header and said ingress is NGINX 1.21 with internal lua module for decoding. Attached example header in ticket.

SRE (Omar): Reproduced locally by sending encoded header through a test ingress; confirmed nginx-lua unescape_uri is decoding percent-encoding before proxying. Tentative fix: disable unescape step and let Redwood claim sanitizer handle decoding consistently, OR update sanitizer to preserve suffix tokens when delimiter characters present.

Support (Leah): Workaround proposed to customer: update ingress lua to not call unescape_uri on X-Auth-Assertion, or configure their IdP to avoid percent-encoding the namespace delimiter until after proxy. Customer evaluating quick change.
Customer (Maya): Applied temporary ingress change to bypass decode and reported admin access restored for impacted users (confirmed via Console).
resolution: Root cause: on-prem ingress was pre-decoding percent-encoded role delimiters (e.g., %2F) and a downstream sanitizer in Redwood's RBAC pipeline was splitting and dropping suffix segments, causing role mismatch. Fix path: 1) Short-term workaround applied by customer — remove/disable the lua unescape_uri call in their ingress for X-Auth-Assertion headers (validated: admin access restored). 2) Medium-term: Redwood will harden the claim sanitizer to preserve namespace suffixes and treat percent-encoded delimiters as first-class tokens (GH PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth/pull/278). 3) SRE guidance page updated with ingress recommendations for private deployments (link added to Confluence). Ticket status: Monitoring in Progress until customer's changes stabilize for 48h. Follow-up: Audit other customers for similar ingress lua usage and ship sanitizer patch in next minor release.
